Two-part staged-opt scratch GATE patch:

PART 1 (Production opt_id gate): Added `int opt_id = -1` to all 4 staged-opt sub-sizer functions in each of the 3 megakernel headers (dec/vit/mb _tc_opt_reduce_floats/_looksam_floats/_muon_floats/_sg2_floats). Each function early-returns 0 when opt_id >= 0 and the runtime opt does not consume that region: opt_reduce gates on Prodigy, muon on Muon, looksam on {LookSAM,SG11,SG15,SG2}, sg2 on SuperGrok2. Also added `int opt_id = -1` to the aggregate `*_tc_staged_opt_floats` and `*_tc_workspace_floats` functions, which pass it through to sub-sizers. The 3 launcher TUs updated: main launcher passes runtime `opt_id`, SG2 launcher passes `static_cast<int>(OptId::SuperGrok2)`. Kernel pointer-carve in all 3 megakernels updated to pass `static_cast<int>(Opt)` to each sub-sizer so host-sizer == device-carve. Decoder kernel has special `if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok2)` for `wbf_f` derivation to avoid computing a pointer from sg2_ws_base (which is dead space for non-SG2 opts).

PART 2 (BUG-04 — Mamba missing kMbStagedOptScratch): Added `kMbStagedOptScratch` compile-time gate gated on `#if SG_MB_BENCH_LAYOUT` (false at bench, true in production), mirroring decoder's `kDecStagedOptScratch`. All 4 mamba staged-opt sub-sizers now return 0 when `!kMbStagedOptScratch` (the bench path). This fixes the missing gate that caused mamba d=1024 bench layout to over-allocate ~199GiB vs the expected ~13.4GiB.

Both parts byte-identical: kernel regions behind `if constexpr (Opt == OptId::LookSAM/Muon/SG2)` are dead code for non-matching opts, so their pointer values (which now land at 0-offset) never affect outputs.

authored.fix: BUG-INT32: Widened the cumulative param-offset arrays from `const int*` to `const int64_t*` throughout the full ABI chain (device kernels, host launchers, dispatch tables, host scratch tensors, Python codegen templates). The primary correctness defect was in `model_stages.cuh` (both sm_90 and gfx942) where `const int n = sizes[t], off = offsets[t]` assigned the offset into an `int` variable before any int64 cast, silently truncating values above 2^31. Both `fused_megakernel.cuh` and the AMD twin had a redundant `(int64_t)` cast that was reading from an `int*` array (safe but type-incorrect at the source). Fixed: (1) all device-stage function signatures + kernel signature now take `const int64_t* offsets`; (2) `model_stages.cuh` + `.hip.hpp` now read directly `const int64_t base64 = offsets[t]` with no int intermediate; (3) `dispatch.cpp` allocates the offsets scratch tensor as `torch::kInt64` and calls `data_ptr<int64_t>()`; (4) all 33 generated `.cu` and `.hip` cell launcher signatures updated; (5) `megakernel_codegen.py` templates updated so regenerated cells also emit the widened type; (6) `check_total_params()` guard added to codegen. Sizes arrays stay int32 (no single tensor exceeds int32). Byte-identical at current scales (offset values fit int32; int64 storage is numerically identical).

Authored the decoder P1-epilogue-fusion lever under knob SG_TUNED_DEC_EPI_FUSE (default 0 = OFF = byte-identical) in csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh. Two independent #if-gated folds inside dectc_forward_tile, each with its own sub-knob defaulting to the master (so fold A can revert alone via -DSG_TUNED_DEC_EPI_FUSE=1 -DSG_TUNED_DEC_EPI_FUSE_A=0, and vice versa):

FOLD B (SG_TUNED_DEC_EPI_FUSE_B) — ff0_b + dec_gelu + X_gact: new thin wrapper dectc_gemm_fwd_f32_ff0fuse reuses tc_gemm_block_unpipelined unchanged; its out() lambda computes pre = v + ff0_b[n0+n] from the exact fp32 wgmma accumulator v (the same value the standalone dectc_gemm_fwd_f32 wrote to sc.work), then writes ff0pre[m,j]=bf16(pre) (LOCAL rows) and X_gact[(g0+m),j]=bf16(dec_gelu(pre)) (GLOBAL rows). BYTE-IDENTICAL transport-only: no reduction-order change, both bf16 rounds bit-for-bit the post-loop's. sc.work is dead between the ff0 GEMM and the ff2 GEMM overwrite (the bwd reads sc.ff0pre, not sc.work), and the LN reduce's sc.work use is untouched.

FOLD A (SG_TUNED_DEC_EPI_FUSE_A) — in_b qkv-bias: new wrapper dectc_gemm_fwd_bias mirrors dectc_gemm_fwd; its bf16-output lambda does __float2bfloat16(v + in_b[n0+n]) — SINGLE round vs the shipping post-loop's bf16(bf16(v)+in_b) DOUBLE round. Sub-bf16-ULP change in the absorbable direction toward the pinned oracle qkv=bf(x_in@bf(in_w)^T+in_b); gate-arbitrated (must land within 1e-4 + pass A/A/A or revert alone).

Both folds reuse the maxed tc_gemm_block_unpipelined engine; the LN reduce is untouched (sc.work still materialized identically).
